core_obligations: (1) implies (2) (proof lines 2241-2249): a nonzero object has a smallest nonzero subobject by the Artinian property, and that subobject is simple; extending a chain by a minimal larger subobject makes the successive quotient simple, and the Noetherian property makes the process terminate after finitely many steps.

(2) implies (1) (proof lines 2251-2256): the author proves the statement by induction on the length n of the filtration; the case n = 1 is the observation that a simple object is both Artinian and Noetherian, and the induction step uses the short exact sequence with the last step of the filtration as subobject and the simple quotient, together with the two companion lemmas on chain conditions in short exact sequences.
proof_roadmap: Use the Artinian and Noetherian hypotheses to build a finite filtration with simple successive quotients.
Induct on the length of a given filtration.
Apply the two chain-condition lemmas to the resulting short exact sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes objects of finite length, that is objects that are simultaneously Artinian and Noetherian, as those admitting a finite filtration whose successive quotients are simple (statement lines 2228-2238). The proof is a complete argument in both directions: the Artinian property produces the smallest nonzero subobject and minimal extensions give the simple quotients, while the Noetherian property stops the process (proof lines 2241-2249); the converse is an induction on the length of the filtration whose base case is that a simple object satisfies both chain conditions and whose step applies two named lemmas on chain conditions in short exact sequences (proof lines 2251-2256). The non-formal content is the construction of the chain of minimal extensions. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
